title: ioctl structure layouts that vary across caller ABIs
summary: Source-backed research candidate for a recurring semantic dependency. No active KOLVRT consumer, compatibility implementation or measured cost is claimed.

history.linux_behavior: Some ioctl arguments vary in pointer width, integer width or alignment between caller ABIs and require compatibility conversion; changing published commands can break applications.
history.historical_reason: Extensible device commands preserve existing application contracts across architecture and interface evolution.
history.root_cause: Published layouts couple request interpretation to caller ABI; untyped command transport alone cannot establish typed native authority.
history.unknown_origin_reason: The pinned documentation establishes the described behavior, not its first introducing release/commit. Historical origin requires separate investigation.

sources.title: Linux v6.12: driver-api/ioctl.rst
sources.locator: Interface versions; 32-bit compat mode; Structure layout
sources.limitations: Pinned documentation reviewed; original introduction/publication date, representative driver users and historical causality remain unverified.

native.behavior: Native messages declare widths, bounds, versions and initialization; new capability types require demonstrated authority differences. No generic native ioctl escape hatch is admitted.
native.why_differs: A compatibility decoder must identify the exact command/layout and call a narrow native operation without passing arbitrary opcodes or issuing extra authority.

security_impact: Validate the same owned snapshot used for execution; distinguish scalars from pointers and preserve native caller/effect scope.
complexity_impact: Each actual ABI pair needs layout tests; command count is neither capability count nor driver coverage.

support.owner_unknown_reason: No supported implementation/consumer owner has been assigned.
support.migration_target: Migrate named consumers to explicit versioned native operations; support only reviewed command/layout pairs while obligations remain.
support.migration_strategy: Identify named consumers and the accepted native contract before proposing compatibility; native rewrite or deferral remain options.
support.removal_condition: No implementation currently exists. Any future implementation needs finite support, named consumers including offline/archival paths and proven quiescence; retain this historical record even if the candidate is rejected.
